ABSTRACT: Confinement of hydrocarbons in nanoscale pockets and pores provides tunable capability for controlling molecules in catalysts, sorbents, and membranes for reaction and separation applications. While computation of the enthalpic interactions of hydrocarbons in confined spaces has improved, understanding and predicting the entropy of confined molecules remains a challenge. Here we show, using a set of nine aluminosilicate zeolite frameworks with broad variation in pore and cavity structure, that the entropy of adsorption can be predicted as a linear combination of rotational and translational entropy. The extent of entropy lost upon adsorption is predicted using only a single material descriptor, the occupiable volume ( $ V_{occ} $). Predictive capability of confined molecular entropy permits an understanding of the relation with adsorption enthalpy, the ability to computationally screen microporous materials, and an understanding of the role of confinement on the kinetics of molecules in confined spaces.

The enthalpy and the entropy contributions to the Gibbs free energies were calculated at T = 298 K and partial pressure of 1 atm (101325 Pa). The enthalpy (H) of gas-phase pyridine and acetonitrile molecules is defined as the sum of total electronic energy ( $ E_{el} $), internal vibrational energy ( $ E_{v} $), zero-point vibrational energy (ZPVE), as well as the rotational and translational contributions to the internal energy: $ H = E_{el} + E_{v} + ZPVE + E_{R} + E_{t} $. The corresponding calculated entropies (S) includes translational, ( $ S_{t} $) vibrational, ( $ S_{v} $) and rotational ( $ S_{r} $) degrees of freedom: $ S = S_{t} + S_{v} + S_{r} $. All the considered systems are in singlet state, thus the electronic contribution to the entropy is zero. The first attempts to describe guest-induced flexibility in zeolites were done using molecular dynamics simulations. $ ^{79-82} $ Rigid zeolitic force fields were dynamically modified using transition state theory to include lattice flexibility, and the results obtained by these models were in good agreement with experimental data. $ ^{79-81,83,84} $ It was shown that framework flexibility in silicalite-1 (MFI-type framework) is responsible for the adsorption of large molecules such as isobutane and heptane with inflection behavior at high loadings, $ ^{80} $ while enhanced self-diffusivity at low loadings of short alkanes (i.e. methane and n-butane) was observed. $ ^{81} $ Framework flexibility is also crucial for aromatics adsorption on MFI zeolite, especially at high pressures. $ ^{84,85} $ While the use of rigid zeolitic models led to the underestimation of the aromatics adsorption in MFI zeolite by a factor of two, $ ^{84,85} $ the use of flexible models to simulate diffusion coefficients of various alkanes in silicalite-1 zeolite resulted in a convergence of experimental and theoretical values. $ ^{86} $ Recently by using in situ integrated differential phase contrast scanning transmission electron microscopy (iDPC-STEM) while adsorbing benzene molecules on MFI zeolite, Xiong et al. showed that the MFI structure goes through severe deformations giving another proof of guest-induced flexibility in zeolites (see Fig. 4). $ ^{87} $

2.4.4. Trapdoor. Traditional diﬀusion models primarily consider two types of interactions: those between guest molecules (guest–guest) and those between guest molecules and the zeolite framework (guest–host). However, when cations are present in the zeolite structure, a third interaction—involving guest molecules, the framework, and cations (guest–host-cation)—must also be accounted for. A striking example of such ternary interactions is the well-known ‘‘molecular trapdoor’’. This phenomenon, also referred to as the ‘‘gating effect’’, describes a unique molecular sieving mechanism in certain zeolites and related porous materi- als. Here, extra-framework cations function as dynamic gate- keepers at pore apertures, selectively controlling molecular diffusion to achieve highly discriminative adsorption and separation.9,147,187 To date, ‘‘trapdoor’’ has been observed in several zeolites, including RHO (DNL-6),188–190 CHA (SAPO-34, SSZ-13),147,191,192 MWF (ZSM-25),149,193 HEU (Clinoptilolite),194

descriptor_candidates.name: occ_vol_confinement_ratio
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss (normalized by R) correlates positively with the ratio of gravimetric occupiable volume to the cube root of molecular volume: adsorbates that fit loosely relative to pore volume retain more gas-like entropy, so this single ratio should lower MAE versus the 14-input network baseline when tested on held-out zeolite/adsorbate pairs.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference from E01/E03: confinement entropy loss scales with how tightly the molecule packs into the occupiable volume; a loose fit preserves translational freedom. The cube root of Vol gives a length scale, so AV/length is a dimensionless-like confinement ratio on source scales.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If replacing the network's inputs with this single descriptor (added or substituted) does not reduce MAE of s_ads/s_gas entropy loss below the full-14-input baseline MAE on cross-validation, the hypothesis is rejected.

descriptor_candidates.name: shape_anisotropy_confinement
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss increases when molecular span exceeds pore-limiting dimensions: a channel-matched anisotropy factor (molecular elongation weighted by the ratio of straight to periodic pore diameters) predicts entropy loss better than occupiable volume alone, because elongated molecules in narrow one-dimensional channels lose rotational entropy disproportionately (TON-like frameworks show largest loss, FAU-like cages smallest, per E01).
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Mechanism: rotational freedom is quenched when the molecule's longest dimension is comparable to the free-sphere diameter (PBF) relative to pore apertures (lsd_f, lsd_p). The log of span-to-brat-least-radius captures elongation; the lsd ratio distinguishes 1D channel from cage frameworks. Source evidence E01/E05 establishes the size/shape-selectivity regime; the specific combination is inference.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Reject if MAE with this descriptor is not lower than the occupiable-volume-only descriptor's MAE, or if residuals show no framework-class dependence (channel vs cage) as predicted.

descriptor_candidates.name: asphericity_density_product
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss is jointly governed by molecular asphericity (normalized third principal moment, capturing near-spherical vs rod-like shape) and framework surface-to-volume density (ASA per pore volume): near-spherical molecules in high surface-density frameworks lose the most entropy, and this product term should reduce MAE relative to models using either shape or porosity alone.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference: spherical molecules can rotate only if cages exceed a critical size (shape term); high accessible-surface per unit pore volume indicates strong wall proximity, increasing confinement friction (density term, used on source numerical scale without unit reassignment). The saturating exp term models diminishing returns of surface area. Source evidence E01 (framework-dependent loss) and E05 (shape selectivity) support the regime; the multiplicative PMI–ASA/AV form is a new combination.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Reject if the interaction term does not improve cross-validated MAE versus its two factors used separately, or if the sign of the PMI3/PMI1+PMI2+PMI3 coefficient is not positive in the fitted entropy-loss direction.

descriptor_candidates.name: pore_gap_asymmetry_entropy
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss is maximal when the pore-limiting diameter (lsd_f) only slightly exceeds the molecular free-sphere radius (PBF), i.e. a small positive aperture-molecule gap, and this gap effect is amplified in frameworks with high volumetric packing density (Vol per occupiable volume). Adding this aperture-matching descriptor should reduce cross-validated MAE of entropy loss/R below the retained shape_anisotropy_confinement MAE (~0.572).
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Mechanism (inference from E01/E05): when the aperture gap (lsd_f - PBF) is small, translational and rotational modes are strongly quenched at channel windows; when the gap is large (cages, FAU-like), gas-like entropy is partly retained. The square compresses negative-gap cases (sterically hindered) while log keeps the term bounded. The volumetric packing factor distinguishes tight 1D channels from open cages, extending E03's occupiable-volume-only relation with an explicit aperture-molecule mismatch term.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Reject if the descriptor's MAE on held-out zeolite/adsorbate pairs is not lower than the retained descriptor's MAE, or if residuals correlate positively (rather than negatively) with the (lsd_f - PBF) gap, contradicting the predicted monotonic decrease of entropy loss with gap size.

descriptor_candidates.name: moment_tortuosity_compaction
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss peaks when the molecular middle-to-smallest principal-moment ratio matches the framework's GeDi-to-periodic-diameter ratio (a shape-pore commensurability condition), with a monotonic correction from framework compaction (density per accessible surface). This commensurability descriptor should lower MAE versus the retained anisotropy descriptor because it captures the matched-dimension regime where rotational freezing is complete, not merely elongation.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Mechanism (inference from E01/E09): rotational entropy loss is most complete when all molecular rotational axes are simultaneously constrained, which occurs at shape-pore commensurability (near-equal dimensionless ratios) rather than at maximum elongation; E09 shows molecular symmetry governs confined dynamics. The exp(-abs(difference)) form is maximal exactly at commensurability. The density/ASA term (source numerical scale, no unit reassignment) proxies wall proximity per surface site. Source evidence establishes framework- and shape-dependence; the specific commensurability form is inference.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Reject if cross-validated MAE does not improve on the retained descriptor's MAE, or if the descriptor shows no peak behavior: i.e., if entropy loss is monotonically related to the raw ratio difference rather than peaking at commensurability (difference near zero).

descriptor_candidates.name: labute_span_window_saturation
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss scales with molecular surface contact opportunity per channel length (LabuteASA divided by span times aperture) but is gated by a sigmoidal window-passage factor: molecules whose free-sphere diameter (PBF) exceeds the periodic pore diameter (lsd_p) relative to GeDi sit in deep, immobile adsorption wells and lose nearly all translational entropy, whereas freely diffusing molecules retain more. This gated contact descriptor should reduce MAE below the retained anisotropy descriptor.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Mechanism (inference from E01/E06/E08): E06's reduced translational/rotational degree corrections for confined molecules and E01's framework-dependent losses suggest two multiplicative factors — contact area per confinement length (surface-guest coupling strength) and a passage gate distinguishing trapped (window-blocked, rattling) from mobile adsorption states; E08 indicates framework flexibility partially relaxes the gate for near-critical molecules, motivating the smooth sigmoid rather than a hard cutoff. Source evidence establishes the regimes; the specific Labute-ASA gating form is a new inference.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Reject if MAE is not below the retained descriptor's MAE on cross-validation, or if partitioning test residuals by the sigmoid gate shows no bimodal (trapped vs mobile) structure in entropy loss, i.e., if the gate factor contributes nothing beyond the contact term alone.

descriptor_candidates.name: interdimensional_ratio_confine
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss grows with the square of the straight-to-periodic pore diameter ratio (a tortuosity/cage-vs-channel proxy) scaled by a molecular volume-to-surface length scale (Vol/LabuteASA)^(1/3). Frameworks where the periodic diameter is much smaller than the straight diameter force molecules through tight windows between larger cavities, quenching extra rotational entropy beyond what occupiable volume alone captures; this descriptor should reduce cross-validated MAE of entropy loss/R below the retained pore_gap_asymmetry_entropy MAE (~0.5521).
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Mechanism (inference from E01/E09): TON-like frameworks show the largest entropy loss (E01), and cavity-window alternation compounds rotational freezing when molecules must reorient at each window crossing (E09 shows rotational-translational coupling under confinement). The (Vol/surface)^(1/3) term is a molecular size length scale in angstroms, making the pair dimensionally coherent with pore diameters; the log of the squared ratio distinguishes stepped (cage-window) from uniform channel topologies. E01/E09 establish the regime; the specific ratio-volume form is a new combination, not a published relation.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Reject if MAE is not lower than the retained descriptor's MAE on held-out pairs, or if residual analysis shows entropy loss does not increase monotonically with the lsd_f/lsd_p ratio among frameworks of similar occupiable volume (e.g., FAU vs MFI-like pairs), contradicting the cavity-window mechanism.

descriptor_candidates.name: packing_saturation_window_fit
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss peaks when the sum of molecular free-sphere diameter and geometric diameter (PBF + GeDi, a two-molecule 'double-occupancy' window width) matches the periodic pore diameter lsd_p — i.e., when a second molecule can barely accompany the first through a window — and this commensurability effect is amplified in compact frameworks (density per occupiable volume). Including this packing-commensurability gate should lower MAE below the retained descriptor, distinguishing single-file dense-loading regimes from isolated-molecule regimes.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Mechanism (inference from E09/E04/E08): E09 shows correlated, structured motion of co-confined molecules; when a window barely admits molecular pairs, guest-guest ordering and window-passage coordination further suppress entropy beyond single-molecule confinement. The exp(-|difference|/scale) factor is maximal exactly at the packing commensurability threshold, analogous to E04's pore-size-dependent solvent structuring. E08's framework flexibility smooths the threshold, motivating the soft exponential rather than a hard step. The literature establishes pore-size-dependent structuring; this specific packing-gap descriptor is a new inference.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Reject if MAE does not improve over the retained descriptor, or if binning test residuals by |lsd_p - PBF - GeDi| shows no peak of entropy loss near zero difference (i.e., entropy loss varies monotonically with that gap instead of peaking at commensurability).

descriptor_candidates.name: moment_span_asphericity_wallcount
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss scales with the product of three independent shape/wall factors: (i) an intermediate-to-largest principal-moment radius ratio capturing mid-axis flattening (disc-vs-rod discrimination beyond SPAN alone), (ii) span-to-geometric-diameter elongation, and (iii) accessible surface per pore volume, a wall-proximity ('wall count') density on the source numerical scale. Disc-like flattened molecules lose more rotational entropy than rods of equal elongation because all in-plane rotations are quenched simultaneously; adding the mid-axis asphericity factor should reduce MAE below the retained descriptor.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Mechanism (inference from E01/E06/E05): E06 applies reduced rotational degree corrections that depend on how many rotational axes are frozen; E01 shows framework-dependent loss magnitude; E05 shows shape-selective adsorption states. Prior descriptors used elongation (SPAN) or commensurability, but never the PMI2/PMI3 mid-axis shape signature, which separates oblate from prolate confined rotation. The ASA/(AV*10^4) term counts wall contact per unit pore volume on source scales. Established relations are the shape-selectivity regime (known); the oblate/prolate entropy discrimination form is a new combination.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Reject if MAE is not below the retained descriptor's MAE on cross-validation, or if residuals for near-spherical molecules (PMI2^0.5/PMI3^0.5 close to 1) do not show the predicted intermediate entropy loss relative to rods and discs — e.g., if entropy loss depends only on SPAN and is invariant to the PMI2/PMI3 ratio at fixed span.

candidates.name: packing_saturation_window_fit
candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss peaks when the sum of molecular free-sphere diameter and geometric diameter (PBF + GeDi, a two-molecule 'double-occupancy' window width) matches the periodic pore diameter lsd_p — i.e., when a second molecule can barely accompany the first through a window — and this commensurability effect is amplified in compact frameworks (density per occupiable volume). Including this packing-commensurability gate should lower MAE below the retained descriptor, distinguishing single-file dense-loading regimes from isolated-molecule regimes.
candidates.rationale: Mechanism (inference from E09/E04/E08): E09 shows correlated, structured motion of co-confined molecules; when a window barely admits molecular pairs, guest-guest ordering and window-passage coordination further suppress entropy beyond single-molecule confinement. The exp(-|difference|/scale) factor is maximal exactly at the packing commensurability threshold, analogous to E04's pore-size-dependent solvent structuring. E08's framework flexibility smooths the threshold, motivating the soft exponential rather than a hard step. The literature establishes pore-size-dependent structuring; this specific packing-gap descriptor is a new inference.
candidates.falsification_criteria: Reject if MAE does not improve over the retained descriptor, or if binning test residuals by |lsd_p - PBF - GeDi| shows no peak of entropy loss near zero difference (i.e., entropy loss varies monotonically with that gap instead of peaking at commensurability).

candidates.name: moment_span_asphericity_wallcount
candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss scales with the product of three independent shape/wall factors: (i) an intermediate-to-largest principal-moment radius ratio capturing mid-axis flattening (disc-vs-rod discrimination beyond SPAN alone), (ii) span-to-geometric-diameter elongation, and (iii) accessible surface per pore volume, a wall-proximity ('wall count') density on the source numerical scale. Disc-like flattened molecules lose more rotational entropy than rods of equal elongation because all in-plane rotations are quenched simultaneously; adding the mid-axis asphericity factor should reduce MAE below the retained descriptor.
candidates.rationale: Mechanism (inference from E01/E06/E05): E06 applies reduced rotational degree corrections that depend on how many rotational axes are frozen; E01 shows framework-dependent loss magnitude; E05 shows shape-selective adsorption states. Prior descriptors used elongation (SPAN) or commensurability, but never the PMI2/PMI3 mid-axis shape signature, which separates oblate from prolate confined rotation. The ASA/(AV*10^4) term counts wall contact per unit pore volume on source scales. Established relations are the shape-selectivity regime (known); the oblate/prolate entropy discrimination form is a new combination.
candidates.falsification_criteria: Reject if MAE is not below the retained descriptor's MAE on cross-validation, or if residuals for near-spherical molecules (PMI2^0.5/PMI3^0.5 close to 1) do not show the predicted intermediate entropy loss relative to rods and discs — e.g., if entropy loss depends only on SPAN and is invariant to the PMI2/PMI3 ratio at fixed span.

interpretation: Replicates vary LLM proposals on one fixed split, not independent datasets. Novelty is unverified.

retained.name: shape_anisotropy_confinement
retained.hypothesis: Entropy loss increases when molecular span exceeds pore-limiting dimensions: a channel-matched anisotropy factor (molecular elongation weighted by the ratio of straight to periodic pore diameters) predicts entropy loss better than occupiable volume alone, because elongated molecules in narrow one-dimensional channels lose rotational entropy disproportionately (TON-like frameworks show largest loss, FAU-like cages smallest, per E01).

retained.name: pore_gap_asymmetry_entropy
retained.hypothesis: Entropy loss is maximal when the pore-limiting diameter (lsd_f) only slightly exceeds the molecular free-sphere radius (PBF), i.e. a small positive aperture-molecule gap, and this gap effect is amplified in frameworks with high volumetric packing density (Vol per occupiable volume). Adding this aperture-matching descriptor should reduce cross-validated MAE of entropy loss/R below the retained shape_anisotropy_confinement MAE (~0.572).

retained.name: interdimensional_ratio_confine
retained.hypothesis: Entropy loss grows with the square of the straight-to-periodic pore diameter ratio (a tortuosity/cage-vs-channel proxy) scaled by a molecular volume-to-surface length scale (Vol/LabuteASA)^(1/3). Frameworks where the periodic diameter is much smaller than the straight diameter force molecules through tight windows between larger cavities, quenching extra rotational entropy beyond what occupiable volume alone captures; this descriptor should reduce cross-validated MAE of entropy loss/R below the retained pore_gap_asymmetry_entropy MAE (~0.5521).
